catalyst.event: LCII voluntarily withdrew its HSR antitrust notification on 2026-09-04 and refiled on 2026-09-09, restarting the waiting period on the Patrick Industries all-stock merger
catalyst.action: close the LCII long opened 2026-08-21 at 94.00 — the position is a leveraged PATK long with an antitrust option written against it for no premium

thesis: This is an UPDATE closing the LCII long, and the reason is only visible in the filings. LCII is not an independent holding: it agreed on 2026-06-30 to be acquired by Patrick Industries in an all-stock merger at a fixed 1.2440 exchange ratio. At PATK 68.71 that makes LCII worth 1.2440 x 68.71 = 85.48, and LCII closed at 85.60 — a 0.15% PREMIUM to its own deal value. There is no discount to capture. The whole 46% drawdown from 158.75 is PATK falling, and PATK closed 0.31% above its own 150-day low. Holding LCII is holding 1.244 shares of a collapsing acquirer while also writing the deal-break risk for zero compensation.
key_risk: Closing here gives up the upside if PATK bottoms — LCII would rise 1.244x with it, and both names being at 150-day lows is the sort of washout that reverses. The HSR pull-and-refile has no stated reason in the 8-K, so the antitrust read is an inference from the procedure, not from anything the company disclosed.
counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that a pull-and-refile is routine housekeeping that avoids a Second Request, the deal still carries $150M of stated run-rate synergies, and a fixed exchange ratio means the position is a bet on a combined $8.1B-revenue business, not on PATK alone. The answer is arithmetic rather than opinion: at a 0.15% premium to parity the market is paying nothing for that bet, so every share of upside is available in PATK directly at 68.71 without the deal-break tail. The original 94.00 entry implied PATK at 75.56; it is 68.71.

evidence.detail: Read the 2026-09-10 Form 8-K (Items 8.01, 9.01) and the accompanying Form 425: merger agreement dated 2026-06-30; HSR Premerger Notification filed 2026-08-05 by both parties; LCI voluntarily withdrew 2026-09-04 and refiled 2026-09-09, initiating a new HSR waiting period. No reason for the withdrawal is disclosed and no Second Request is mentioned.

Method shown: fixed all-stock exchange ratio 1.2440 PATK per LCII share x PATK close 68.71 = 85.4752 parity value. LCII closed 85.60, a premium of 0.1248 (+0.146%). LCII shareholders take ~48% of the combined company. The position therefore has no arbitrage spread and full acquirer beta.

Both legs sit on their lows: LCII 85.60 is 0.62% above its 150-day low of 85.07 (range 85.07-158.75); PATK 68.71 is 0.31% above its 150-day low of 68.50 (range 68.50-144.29, -52.38% off the high). There is no support beneath either.

thesis: This is an UPDATE closing the NKE long opened 2026-08-17 at 40.75, now -12.9%. Two things changed since the 2026-09-08 exit call that was never acted on. Second, earnings are now confirmed for 2026-09-28. This position carries no stop, so it is an uncapped loss about to be marked by a binary event, which is the one combination worth removing regardless of what you think of the business.
key_risk: Closing at a 150-day low five sessions before a print is selling exactly where a beaten-down name gaps up on any good news, and NKE has fallen far enough that expectations are already low. This is a risk-management exit, not a call that the business is worse than the price.
counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that the April insider buying was a genuine signal from people who know the company, and that the original 62.00 target is a multi-year recovery thesis a single quarter cannot settle. A multi-year thesis also does not require holding an unstopped position through a dated print.
